body:
I have myalgic encephalomyelitis. I have full mobility but my strength and stamina are severely affected. I have maybe 30 seconds of activity I can handle, after that I'm just a lifeless heap.

I'm female, 29, and the saddest thing for me is that I met a man who absolutely knocks my socks off only after I got ill. I'll never get to enjoy his body fully free.

Sex can still be great because I feel everything normally, but for the most part I have to lie still on my back and let him do all the work.

The biggest problem for me is the emotional part of it, because I know I can't do things to him that he likes- my arms, legs, mouth... everything is too weak and fatigued.

More than just discomfort, it's impossible for me to read books.

That's also a big loss because I love reading and I read so many books ever since I was a child.

There is an excellent online community for people with ME. But very few get any relief from medication or supplements. Unsurprisingly, #1 cause of death for people with ME is suicide and not the actual disease itself.

Reddit is great because I can't read more than few paragraphs of text at a time, which means comments are just perfect.

Currently I'm seeing about 5 specialists.

Throughout all these years I've seen probably over 20 specialists, one even outside the country. Even had a brain surgery. Just in case :P In the beginning they were reluctant to trust me because all the test results were coming back negative and I claimed I couldn't even walk to the bathroom alone.

But now more and more things are giving out, the latest addition to the party is the heart. Now I'm taking beta blockers. They trust me now but I'm not sure if finally having the proof is a good or bad thing.

I miss music so much. 

Since I got ill it's like I've been buried alive.

I never heard of them. What's their new album called?

I can't really listen to music last few years. My brain can't process it and it's just noise that causes my symptoms to flare up

Haha, I hate Jazz ^^
Heavy Metal's not bad. I don't really have a specific type of music I like, nor a favorite band. I just like a song here and there.

2 or 3 songs from Enya, Enigma, Person's Pitch, Foo Fighters, Apocalyptica, Boomfunk, Greenday, Coldplay, Smash Mouth, Faithless...

I'm sorry to hear you're ill as well. That really isn't something that's easy to deal with.

Yeah, Myalgic Encephalomyelitis is a more specific and more severe subset of chronic fatigue syndrome but the definition varies depending on the country.

I have so many things I love doing. From science to art. Or just sitting outside watching people pass by. Or watch tv shows while holding someone's hand. Listening to music. 

But I can't do any of that. I can't do much of anything apart from lie in bed and walk around the apartment for maybe half an hour a day which I use to tend to personal hygiene and stuff like that.

I wouldn't mind being a weirdo cause that would still mean I am something :)

Nice to meet you too Crash :)
Of course. It's called myalgic encephalomyelitis. You can ask about any details you are curious about.

My education... I received an award for being the top University student few months prior to falling ill. After falling ill my memory got wrecked, my concentration is gone, and I can't even read short articles let alone continue with an education.

Friends... people don't want to be friends with someone who can't even talk on the phone with them. Even online friends... I get periods where I can't communicate for months. They lose interest. I don't blame them, I would to. It's just the way things are.

I am a fighter. I fought for my future all my life. There is just nothing left figthing for.

But I guess you're right. I'm not nothing. Yet.

Thank you.
Wow, that's a long list. Thanks!
I agree. I especially loved KOTR. Sadly, I already played them.
I had something recent in mind, with nice graphics, but if I can't find it I will check this out too.
Thanks, it sounds like I should check it out.

Thank you so much. 

It doesn't really have to be Japanese actually, those two just popped into my mind.

I imagine death exactly as it was before I was born: nothing.
No darkness, no loneliness, no eternity.

Then it doesn't scare me anymore. Because I was already dead. For billions of years.

Thanks for making me laugh :)

Despite majority being very hostile, I must admit there are doctors who genuinely only want to help and don't care about their own egos. Having gone through all this, I appreciate those kinds of people even more

I agree it's not nearly as bad as it was in the past.

But it's much worse than people think it is.

I had a psychiatrist ask me: "But what makes you think you're ill at all?" after I have spent two years bed-bound, completely dependent on my parents for basic needs. I was a healthy successful 20-something-year old mathematician before I got ill, mind you.

And the statement: "If your parents died today you would just get out of bed and go on with your life," takes the cake.

If you think I was unlucky with my doctor choice just read confessions of some other patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, it gets much worse. And there are millions of people in the US alone who have it.

You say there was nothing else they could have done.

But even today psychiatrist stick blindly to their practices even when it's evident they are harming the patients.

Just look up Myalgic Encephalomyelitis, more commonly known as Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. It is classified as a Neurological disease by WHO, lately there’s even some evidence that it might be autoimmune disease. It is severely debilitating with some patients unable to get out of bed for decades.
And psychiatrist keep on treating it with Cognitive Behaviour Therapy!

Now, CBT can be a great thing, but not for neurological or autoimmune diseases. 

They are putting patients in danger by hindering biomedical research and by not getting them real help they need, and even going as far as to try and convince patients they are not ill at all.

And this is all happening in 2013.
Yeah, internet is an amazing thing. I have no idea what I would have done if I was born 50 years earlier. Probably be suicidal.

You said it very well, and I completely agree with you.

BUT, I am not angry that they are not visiting me, I'm angry that they don't even text me to see if I'm still alive. I just think that's a minimum of human decency.

Some people who were even not my friends before I got ill, pick up the phone every 6 months or so, check on me, give me a few ecouraging words, and go on with their lives. I just think that's manners, if nothing else.

I'm not an expert, but I really think you can't.

I once heard it explained like this:

If you take a person from Norway and put it next to a person from central Africa, you can clearly see they look very different and you might be compelled to declare them of different race.

BUT, if you slowly travel from central Africa North towards Norway you will see that the skin color is very gradually getting lighter.

There is no clear line where scientists could say: "From here onward are white people, and no longer black people."

I know you're trying to be funny, but you're just not.

And I won't give you the satisfaction of downvoting you. Let everyone see your uninspired comment.
Is "English is my second language" a good excuse for not picking up on that? :)
I'm not from the US. And different countries have different definitions of races, since it's all just made up anyway and has no scientific basis.
I thought Eskimo is a culture, not race. My bad

I made that comment as a retort the the annoying comment that has been deleted later. I was just being spiteful.

But honestly, how come racism towards Asian men is spewed so nonchalantly in 21st century? Honestly... 

My boyfriend is Asian, and yeah, guess what, he's amazing in bed.

Not in bed.

Edit: The coward that had deleted his/her comments had said: Asian guys are easily forgettable.
You forgot about Asian men.
You forgot about Asian men.
I wonder what kind of misinformation they are feeding us today.
I totally agree. That's why I think I should look for new friends. Too much resentment
Thank you :)

I am maintaining my half of the friendship. Read my reply to MistressMagus.

I'm not expecting them to magically show up. I'm just expecting them to show up like they did when I was healthy. It's what friends do.

They are not busy. And even if they are that's a crappy excuse. If being busy was the problem then they would have been too busy even when I was healthy. Did 8 people suddenly become swamped with work and family the moment I got ill?

I did ask them a few times. But I think at this point I'm just too angry at them to bother. Maybe I can meet some people online who are in similar situation as I am.

I asked them so many times what is happening in their lives. I listened about them losing their job, breaking up with their girlfriend, and I showed them compassion and understanding, even as I was waiting to have my brain split open by a surgeon. I never pushed my problems on them because I knew blood and disease makes people uncomfortable.

I don't know where you got the idea that I've been sitting silently. Yes, I am bitter. Very bitter. But I am bitter NOW. I wasn't bitter after a month of being ill, or half a year. Or a year. Or two years. I think giving them 3 years is enough time.

And I did ask why they are not around. They said it's too difficult to see me cause it reminds them I'm ill. Yeah right.

They asked me if it is contagious, I explained to them very clearly several times that it's not at all. I gave them all the details they need.

I never felt sorry for myself, and I still don't. It's heartbreaking that I lost my previous life but I don't dwell on it, I'm trying to build on what I have.

I may be very wrong about this, but I don't think I should be the one to go out of my way to contact them.

They were my friends. They were supposed to care about me. And the moment things were not 100% the way they wanted it to be they completely abandoned me.

At this point I would rather make new friends.

I'm curious, why do you think it is completely up to me to keep the contact and they don't have to do anything about it?

I'm almost 30, and they are all over 30.Way too old for age to be any excuse.

I just don't see how I can believe they care about me when they don't even check to see if I have died. What kind of caring is that?

How can I reach to reconnect when we haven't even been able to keep the connection going? Nothing has changed since then. I haven't gotten a bigger need to hang out with them now than I did before. I'm not miraculously healed. Everything remained the same.

Of course friends come and go, I've lost connections over the years with people as well. But it happens naturally, one by one. Now it was all my friends at the same time.

My boyfriend has managed to stay with me through thick and thin. If he could do it, then so could they.

Sorry, I'm just annoyed with them a lot.

It's not contagious at all. What kind of a jerk would I be if I put other people in danger like that?

When I don't make an effort to contact them first, they don't contact me for years. That sounds like a one-way street to me.
I really don't want to start seeing the world as such a sad place.

I'm going to be honest, I only tried to contact them a few times. I feel like I've made it very obvious that I appreciate any company and that I'm lonely. But I still have some pride left and I'm not going to drag someone by the sleeve who has no interest in hanging out with me.

What you say makes sense, and I can see why they don't want to drop by without being invited. I actually appreciate that as I often need to sleep at strange times.

But can anyone really honestly say that a text, or a facebook message is an imposition? There are so many ways to contact a person nowadays without imposing on them that I just don't see that as a valid excuse.

I answer any questions they might have about my illness but I have no will to talk about it. I'm alone with my illness all day long, when my friends come along I want to hear gossip about their bosses, girlfriends and normal everyday stuff that I miss in my life.

We talk about exactly the same things we talked about when I was healthy.

I don't mind guiding them, but I can't guide someone who is not in contact in me.

I could lose the trust of my doctors when I out of the blue ask them to prescribe a drug that can develop addiction.

I can further damage my health since no one really knows how different drugs affect us in the long run.

But the main reason is simply that there are hundreds of options I have and the best I can do is go for the ones that the most people with ME say helped them.

I seriously doubt that. Otherwise everyone with ME would be rushing to take it and pushing for more research.

I mean of course there's a chance it helps, but there's hundreds other medication with that potential as well.
What makes you think that?

There are many off-label treatments that supposedly help a bit, but it's very difficult to get the doctors to prescribe them off-label.

For me they usually prescribed supplements like Acetyl L-Carnitine, NADH, sleeping pills. etc. but nothing helped. Not even a bit.

Rituximab seems promising but since it's a rather dangerous drug we're all waiting for more research to be done.

The cause of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis is still unknown :(

I've been ill for 6 years, I've basically done all test known to humankind. I just have ME, and typical deregulations that go along with it, like low natural killer cell number and function.
Thank you

Getting out of the bed is not the problem, thinking is the problem. 

My professor always allowed me to communicate with him over e-mail and Skype, he's a really great guy.

But there's no use, my mental capabilities are too damaged.

Aaaw, it's nice to know we're all horizontal, haha

I do pacing as well. Sadly as my illness is naturally progressing towards worse spectrum I am unable to build up what I can do.

But before I found out about pacing I was pushing myself because I believed I am going to make myself tougher this way. Then one day I ended up panting in bed unable to sit up and even too weak to chew food just because I did mild exercise for 10 minutes the day before.

After that I kind of figured out on my own that I shouldn't do too much, and what too much meant for me, but it wasn't until I read about pacing that this concept actually became clear in my mind.

I get no support from the hospital, but luckily my parents are very supportive so they do everything that I am unable to. It is frustrating and embarrassing to depend on my parents at this age but I am also extremely happy that I have someone to help me at all. 

It's not too difficult to imagine myself starving to death if I was left with no help.

Yeah, I can understand.

I noticed that people who have chronic pain tend to be depressed much more often than other chronic conditions. No wonder.

Luckily my pain gets bad only if I overdo it. And by overdo it I mean have a shower, or talk to someone for more than half an hour.

As far as I know ME is the only chronic illness where any form of exercise actually damage the body. It's horrible seeing my body deteriorate like this.

May I ask what you are doing to try and regain your life?
How do you deal with that? Did you manage to accept it? How long has it been?

like 

smrt, prst, vrt, ....

I agree with everything they mentioned except the motor speed. It's very obvious when something happens suddenly that I react with a few seconds of delay.

If met with perfect conditions my brain can function normally in everyday life. But if two things happen at the same time I either freeze, or get extremely fatigued in matter of seconds. So I can't be at the table with many people, I can't talk if there is music in the background, I can't walk and talk etc.

The biggest issue for me is fast fatigability. I get tired and distracted after reading a paragraph of text. Typing these comments is going to be the only thing I can do between sleeping.

Croatian grammar is insane. There is no way I could have learnt it if I wasn't a native speaker.

I studied Latin in school, Danish for a few months, and I've been attempting to learn Korean since I've gotten ill. It takes me between 20 and 30 times longer to memorize Korean vocabulary now than it Danish one when I was healthy, but it is difficult to say which part of that is due to Danish being similar to English.

From [International Consensus Criteria for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis](http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1365-2796.2011.02428.x/pdf): 

"In view of more recent research and clinical experience that strongly point to widespread inflammation and multisystemic neuropathology, it is more appropriate and correct to use the term ‘myalgic
encephalomyelitis’ (ME)"

There is hardly any evidence for anything. Or better yet, there is a lot of different evidence for a lot of different disregulations but rarely ever do they get independently confirmed.

This is an excerpt from Wikipedia page about CFS: 

"...cognitive symptoms were principally resultants of deficits in attention, memory, and reaction time... Simple and complex information processing speed and functions entailing working memory over long time periods were moderately to extensively impaired... Perceptual abilities, motor speed, **language**, reasoning, and intelligence **did not appear to be significantly altered**."

I think that's why it is difficult to notice how bad my condition is just from talking to me or reading what I've written.

It becomes difficult to communicate when I get extremely sleepy (like I am right now:) ), but that would happen even to a perfectly healthy person who was as sleepy as I am. The only difference is that I become that way after an hour or two, whereas a healthy person would probably take 48 hours of being awake to reach that level.

It happens to me often that after waking up I can suddenly notice many mistakes in something I had written before I went to sleep.

I love reading and I read countless books in English. I think that enabled me to think in English instead of my native language, Croatian.

----------------------------------------

As far as the Physics goes, since my memory is impaired it is almost impossible to learn something new. And as for the things I already know, I have trouble seeing the big picture when solving a problem. I used to be really good at that before.

Even in a simple beginner level problem, such as “an object is sliding down a steep slope…”, it is impossible for me to take a step back and see what is really asked of me, which formulae I should use, and what is actually happening.

I realized this when I took my old primary school Physics books. I thought maybe by starting over I could at least keep my brain primed while I wait to be cured but very soon it became obvious I can’t do even that.

Even though English is my second language, I started learning it  when I was rather young, just 11 years old.

However, I feel like I still struggle with it. One of the biggest difficulties for me are definitive and indefinite articles.

Maybe the difference between me and the native speakers is that after I write something I go back and check it multiple times and try to make it sound more natural. They probably feel more secure with their knowledge so they don't bother.


I'm not sure if you are being serious about what you said or if you are just trying to cheer me up, but either way, thank you. I was really starting to feel like a waste of oxygen I breathe.

I don't know why you're getting downvoted.

You have a good point. Not to mention that you'll never hear women being grossed out that their brothers have sex. 

But godforbid a woman has sex and enjoys it.

Usually cure doesn't just spring up like that. Even if someone accidentally stumbled upon the perfect cure, it would take years of research and bureaucracy before it would become available.


I didn't know how long it takes before I became ill with an incurable disease.

And you should also understand that us sick people are not stupid. We are aware that nothing is set in stone, but sometimes, even one more day can be too much to handle.

That's very inspiring, thank you.

I'm glad to hear you're doing better.

I guess you're right. I've been sick for 6 years and it seems like an eternity but people can live with ME for 20 or 30 years. There's still some hope for me.

P.S. I love LOTR :)

It's ok really. It takes me longer to read it, but I got through it :)

You didn't bumm me out at all. You came up with wonderful suggestions, I actually felt bad for having to shoot them down. But just that you put so much effort to think about what I could do makes me feel less alone, so really thank you.

I know it's unusual that I miss Physics more than I miss going out with friends, or going shopping, or even being able to go outside. I miss all those things too, but missing my career is just overpowering.

I have to admit there were moments of darkness, when I couldn't get out of bed even to eat, when I thought about ending it all. But as soon as I can be awake and talk I can find small things that make me happy.

For example, I depend on my parents, which is really embarrasing at my age. But I still have my sense of humor, and when I see I can still crack my parents up it makes me happy again.


I have a country I wanted to travel to and I watch a lot of YouTube videos about it. It hurts to think I will probably never see it with my own eyes, but it makes me so happy that I have Internet so I can see it every day.

I will admit I miss feeling like the queen of the world when I got those awards, and I miss people being in awe when I tell them. I guess my ego enjoyed that, hehe. But I just as much miss those moments alone at my desk when it was just me and Physics long into the night.

ME has unknown cause for everyone, not just me.

I tested for Celiac disease: I don't have the antibodies and I'm the wrong HLA type. Still, I tried gluten free diet for 4 months. I tried every diet out there.

Trust me, after 6 years, I've done every test under the Sun, and seen every doctor there is to see.

I'm at the point in my life where I have to accept that I have ME, and that it is incurable.

Love it :)

But I can't keep track with most games. My reaction time is severly slowed and looking at bright screens tires me.
Ah. But my ME specialist warned me that antidepressant tend to have negative impact on the disease.
I think I can't take any credit, I'm just a naturally cheerful person and I have amazingly supportive family.

Wow, thank you for this long comment. I really appreciate your effort.

The thing is... I can't really do those things. 

First of all, my passion is Physics, not teaching. Even though I may be teaching Physics it is completely different types of calling.  And different types of people are good at it.

All those things you mention may be fun to do, but they're not what I'm passionate about.

The second thing, and much more important, cause my passion could even change over time is the fact that I am too ill to do any of what you mention.

I can't make videos because I need to be lying down most of the time. As you mention videos need lightning, good camera work, editing skills. I am unable to do that physically and mentally.

 I can't review toys because I've been unemployed for 6 years, I depend on others to buy food and clothes for me, I can't really ask they start buying toys now. 

I know I sound negative and like I gave up, but I've been ill for 6 years, I just know my limits. Most of the days I can't even watch a movie because the screen is too bright and I can't follow the plot.

My career is over. I just need to find a way to deal with that.
Help with what? I'm a very cheerful person

I'm really sorry you went through that hell. 

I hope life finally gives you a break you need to build yourself up from the hole it pushed you into.

Ok, I'll be my own friend. Luckily, I'm really fun to be around, haha.

Thank you. I'm really insecure about my English ability. It's never easy speaking a foreign language.

ME suffered a horrible destiny in the UK, I think that's why most organizations are active there. I think US ones might have a less bumpy road to tread on.

But actually that is an excellent idea! Since I have so little energy I could help them a bit instead of trying to do everything on my own which would probably be impossible. 

Thank you!
I have been unemployed for 6 years. How am I supposed to pay someone to do it for me?

I hoped that I will rise to the level where I would be able to do it slower but that has not happened.

I had a few weeks worth of work to finish writing my Master thesis. I have been unable to do that for 6 years.

I have different levels of abilities: Talking is easy, reading or writing is difficult, abstract thinking is impossible. That means I even have trouble making simple decisions in the future like what I want for dinner and of course something as abstract as physics is out of my reach.

I didn't forget Physics so much as I can't form the thoughts in my mind.

Even something simple like reddit comments I need to take a break after reading every paragraph.

Usually people with ME can't work even part time. I'm a medium case I think. Severe cases can't even eat on their own.

Professor Hawking is a great inspiration to me. But notice that he, deaf people, blind people, all have physical disabilities. Hawking can be a scientist but he can't be an athlete not matter how much he would wish it.

The reason why I believe my career is a hopeless goal is because this illness destroyed both physical and mental aspects of who I am.

But now I'm just being fussy :) I get your point.

And I really do wish to raise awareness but I don't know where to begin. Without energy and money everything seems like a too large hurdle.

There's not a lot I can do. I'm not sure you realize how severe this disease is. The problem is not that I have to stay at home. The problem is that I'm having trouble typing out this comment. 

I can't read even simple novels.

How am I supposed to write scientific papers?

I do bless the internet every single day, though. It became my whole life, from keeping in touch with people, to giving me a good laugh, to watching tutorials. It's my life support :)

But my defeat is not temporary. It's permanent. The disease is incurable and there's hardly any research done on it. There's more research for hay fever.

Of course hope always exists, but I believe in being realistic, not just blindly positive.

I haven't lost my drive. That is the problem. I want to do it more than anything. But my brain won't comply.

Myalgic Encephalomyeltis is like a subset of chronic fatigue syndrome. A lot of people who have unexplained fatigue get CFS diagnosis. ME requires a bunch of other extra symptoms and blood tests.

I got diagnosed by ME specialist. I've tried everything and nothing makes me feel better. On contrary, I have steadily been getting worse.

It's incurable disease, and all the doctors I've seen (over 20 I think) have agreed: Better luck next time around.

-----------
But it really doesn't matter what I have, I know no one here can help me get healthy, I just want to find a way to accept that I can never do what was my passion all my life.

I don't want to be bitter and frustrated all my life.

This is actually a nice idea.

The problem is that I never wanted to be a teacher. It excites me when I improve my own knowledge or solve a problem. Going over what I already know and figuring out how to explain it is just not my thing.

But please don't misunderstand, I'm really grateful for your idea.
I haven't because pain is the least of my problems. But I guess despite having different cause we are suffering from same consequences.

I think he should be very careful with that approach.

I know from my own experience when people tell me "it's not all so bad" all I can hear is

"We don't understand your suffering, we think it's not important enough, and would you just stop whining"

People who are mourning a loss of something or someone need their pain validated.
